newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen futures end weaker, Eurodollar mixed.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen futures end weaker, Eurodollar mixed.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures weakened in thin trade on Thursday dragged lower by dollar/yen pressures and views Japan's economy would remain sluggish early this year.
Trade was slow with Japanese investors away until Monday for a one-week holiday, and Singapore traders mostly absent due to a general election today, a public holiday.
The March Euroyen contract was at 99.44 at 1115 GMT, down from its IMM close of 99.45, and June was at 99.34, down from its settlement of 99.39 previously.
"Euroyen has been dragged lower by strong dollars. It's been follow-through trade and stops being triggered," a dealer said.
Traders said it was easy in the thin market for sellers to push the complex lower, but the downtrend was partly a pullback.
June Euroyen was assessed supported for the near-term at 99.33, and September at 99.17.
The dollar's strength against the yen recently, rising to a 116.28 high on Tuesday, reinforced views Japan's economy would turn around at a slower rate than forecast this year.
Eurodollars were mixed in light trade, hurt by the sharp fall in U.S. treasuries on the last trading day of 1996.
March ended at 94.45 compared with its previous 94.44 IMM close, and June at 94.27, down against 94.28.
Traders said London investors were seen in today's thin market, mostly to adjust positions ahead of U.S. trade.
Strong U.S. economic data caused treasuries to nosedive more than one point on Tuesday, on perception a rosy economy would lead to tighter credit, dealers said.

The market was now eyeing U.S. weekly jobless claims and the National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) December report tonight. Economists polled by Reuters expect claims to edge down to 334,000 in the week ended December 28, from 335,000 a week earlier, another sign of a stronger economy.
